detail: A real release sends a provider request and preserves the controlled answer after browser reload.
Unicode, emoji, paragraphs, and an exact URL survive provider transport and browser reload.
Chat tool calls create two pending definitions. Explicit review accepts each definition.
One browser OAuth sign-in exchanges a PKCE code and attaches two APIs to the resulting grant.
Denied consent records a denied attempt without a token exchange or false connection.
Selecting a second synthetic account creates a distinct grant. Invocation identity remains to be checked.
Current shared account and per-connection labels reach distinct provider tool descriptions after renaming.
An expired shared token refreshes once. Both dependent APIs then return the intended account records. Concurrent refresh remains pending.
Two concurrent production adapter calls refresh one shared grant once and return the correct account.
A model tool selected by its current account label calls the second account while first-account connections remain configured.
Revocation rejects already-saved calls for both dependent APIs before either reaches the fake service.
Disconnecting the shared grant removes both dependent tools. The other account remains available. Active grants prevent application deletion.
